drug_class: Combined Hormonal Oral Contraceptive (Birth Control Pill)
purpose: This medication is a combination birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help regulate your menstrual cycle or reduce menstrual cramps. In some cases, doctors use it to help with acne or other hormone-related conditions.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — a progestin and an estrogen — that work together to prevent pregnancy in a few ways. First, they stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm have a harder time getting through, and they thin the lining of your uterus to make it less likely for a fertilized egg to implant.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, headaches, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods, mood changes, and decreased sex drive. These often improve after the first few months as your body adjusts to the hormones.
warnings: Do not take this pill if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as this raises your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. This medication does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have chest pain, sudden severe headache, vision changes, or leg pain or swelling.
typical_dosing: You take one pill every day, at the same time each day, for 28 days. The pack usually contains 21 active hormone pills and 7 reminder pills (placebo pills). You start a new pack right after finishing the old one without taking a break. Taking it at the same time every day helps it work best and reduces side effects like nausea.
